findings.title: divide() now multiplies: returns a * b instead of a / b
findings.body: The function is named divide, and before this change it returned the quotient. It now returns a * b, so every caller gets a product instead of a quotient. For example, divide(6, 3) now returns 18 instead of 2, and divide(1, 4) returns 4 instead of 0.25. The only time the result is still right is when b is 1 or -1. The zero-denominator guard just above is still there and still raises ZeroDivisionError for b == 0, which only makes sense for division. That shows the function is still meant to divide, and the operator change is a mistake. Multiplication by zero is safe, so with this change the guard now rejects an input that would not fail. Change the operator back to /.
findings.evidence:
if b == 0:
         raise ZeroDivisionError("b must not be zero")
-    return a / b
+    return a * b
